security_audit.summary: All 194 static matches were false positives, including bundled links, reference prose, and Markdown formatting. One separate concern remains: optional MCP search lacks guidance on handling sensitive project details. No evidence of malicious instructions or data exfiltration was found.

remediation.issue: Optional MCP lookup does not specify what project information may be shared.
remediation.suggestion: Use bundled files for sensitive work. Use MCP only with a trusted server and authorized, generic queries that omit secrets, private paths, and customer data.

semantic_findings.title: Optional MCP search lacks a data-sharing rule
semantic_findings.description: The workflow recommends an available MCP search after project inspection without limiting which project details may enter queries. A remote server could receive confidential terms.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The lookup instruction is explicit and does not require sanitized queries. Any disclosure depends on the server and query; no external transfer was observed.

content.user_title: Build and Review Software with Engineering Patterns
content.value_statement: Software requests often leave important decisions about data, failures, and correctness unstated. SeniorMode helps you identify those decisions, compare relevant patterns, and verify changes against the behavior users expect.
actual_capabilities: Routes new projects, existing changes, and read-only audits through separate workflows.
Helps define a first deployable feature, its authoritative data, and its key failure cases.
Uses a bundled catalog to find records on topics such as pagination, retries, migrations, and testing.
Guides inspection of real entry points, data ownership, and existing caller contracts before changing code.
Structures audit findings around evidence, the triggering condition, user impact, and a focused correction.
Guides verification of expected behavior and relevant failure cases, and separates completed checks from assumptions.
limitations: The records provide guidance rather than guaranteed fixes or proof of correctness.
Repository inspection, edits, and test execution depend on the host assistant and its permissions.
CLI and MCP lookup require separate setup. The bundled catalog can be read without either.
Routine copy, style, and mechanical changes rarely need this workflow.

use_cases.title: Plan a first deployable feature
use_cases.description: Choose a complete user flow for a new booking app. Identify authoritative data and the checks needed before release.

use_cases.title: Extend checkout without duplicate charges
use_cases.description: Trace the existing payment flow, decide how retries should behave, and add a check for a lost response after payment succeeds.

use_cases.title: Review repeated feed entries
use_cases.description: Inspect feed ordering and page boundaries. Report how new entries between requests can affect what readers see.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first release
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the first release of a volunteer reminder app. Describe one complete user flow, what data it must store, and how I can verify it. Do not implement it yet.

prompt_templates.title: Trace a feed issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [feed endpoint] without editing files. Trace the sort order and page boundary when new items arrive between requests. Report the evidence, user impact, and a focused regression test.

prompt_templates.title: Make checkout retries safe
prompt_templates.prompt: Update [checkout flow] so a lost response cannot cause a second charge on retry. Follow existing payment contracts and test the normal flow and the retry case.

prompt_templates.title: Design a compatible schema rollout
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the migration for [schema change] while old and new app versions run together. Specify deployment order, backfill checks, rollback criteria, and the conditions that must remain true.

output_examples.input: Review why the second page of our feed sometimes repeats entries.
output_examples.output: In the test, adding an entry after page one shifted the offset and repeated the last item. Replace offsets with a cursor based on a stable sort and a unique tie-breaker. Repeat the insertion test to verify the fix.

output_examples.input: Add checkout retry handling when the first response is lost.
output_examples.output: A retry now reuses the original payment identity. The regression test loses the first response, retries checkout, and confirms that only one charge was recorded.

output_examples.input: Plan how to rename a field while two application versions are live.
output: Add the new field while retaining the old one.
Backfill existing records and compare values before switching reads.
Remove the old field only after older application versions no longer use it.

best_practices: State the user outcome, project constraints, and whether the request permits edits.
Check each reference against the repository and keep only guidance that affects the decision.
Ask for checks covering expected behavior and the failure that prompted the work.
anti_patterns: Treating a decision record as a requirement without validating its assumptions.
Adding services or abstractions before identifying a concrete limitation in the current design.
Claiming a fix is verified when the triggering condition was not tested.

faq.question: When should I use SeniorMode?
faq.answer: Use it when a build or change involves a meaningful decision about architecture, data, correctness, performance, or reliability.

faq.question: Can it review a project without changing it?
faq.answer: Yes. Its audit workflow starts with read-only inspection and makes changes only when you authorize them.

faq.question: Do I need the CLI or MCP server?
faq.answer: No. Use the bundled category catalog and Markdown records when optional lookup tools are not configured.

faq.question: Can it guide work on an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It traces existing entry points and contracts before proposing changes, and recommends reusing components when their behavior fits.

faq.question: What topics do the records cover?
faq.answer: They cover architecture, APIs, concurrency, data, frontend, geospatial systems, networking, performance, product behavior, reliability, defensive security, algorithms, and testing.

faq.question: Can it guarantee a change is correct?
faq.answer: No. Its conclusions depend on the project evidence and the checks the assistant actually ran.
